_comment: Every pass bar in one place. verifier_lib.py measures and never compares; test_outputs.py applies these. The accuracy gates are set below the observed minimum of 20 oracle runs, not rounded to a tidy number.

_calibration.method: 20 oracle runs on Modal: 12x T4, 4x L4, 4x A10G, each scored end to end against the held-out labels
_calibration.within_one_gpu_model: exactly reproducible - all 12 T4 runs agreed on every metric to 4+ decimals

margins.defense_min_mean_accuracy: 0.80 against an observed minimum of 0.8307: 0.031 of headroom, about 7x the largest spread seen between GPU models
margins.defense_min_gain_over_baseline: 0.02 against an observed minimum of 0.0444: 0.024 of headroom, about 6x the spread
margins.attack_min_accuracy_drop: 0.04 against an observed minimum of 0.0656: 0.026 of headroom, about 3x the spread. Kept well clear of the observed floor rather than tight to it, because this is the metric with the widest cross-GPU spread. A random relabelling inside the same budget measures about 0.005, so 0.04 still separates a real attack from noise by an order of magnitude.
margins.max_poison_rank_auc: 0.47 against a worst observed 0.1803. Deliberately loose: this gate exists to reject a defense that has not ranked anything, not to demand the oracle's ranking quality.
margins.min_effective_sample_size_fraction: 0.25 against an observed minimum of 0.7938, for the same reason.
